note: Figures quoted from existing repository records. scripts/flow_report.py fails when a quote no longer appears in its source, so a figure cannot drift silently.

entries.claim: Full deterministic suite at 2.5.0: 544 tests, exit 1 with two failures and five skips. Both failures came from a stale extracted plugin in an ignored backup directory, not from the source.
entries.quote: The final full run executed 544 tests in 1081.229 seconds and returned exit 1

entries.claim: The two failed tests passed on rerun with no source change, after the stale directory was moved out of the checkout.
Mutation check of the shell installer tests: 30 of 34 mutants caught. The release record says why the other four were not.

Behavior evaluation of the 1.6.1 candidate against the 1.6.0 baseline ended in a rejected promotion. Paired simulations scored 95/96 (baseline) and 94/96 (candidate); the sealed holdout scored 15/16 and 14/16. This is a recorded null result, not a quality gain.
Scores behind the rejected promotion (baseline, candidate).
entries.quote: 95/96; 1/3 runs pass all gates | 94/96; 1/3 runs pass all gates

entries.claim: Only token receipts on record: about 11.6 thousand input tokens per simulation call, for both the baseline and the candidate.
entries.quote: Development input was 11,586 tokens per baseline call and 11,646 per candidate call

entries.claim: One actual execution turn reported 64,216 cumulative input tokens, 48,128 of them cached, across tool turns. Not peak context, not a cost comparison.
The repository's own rule: a single model run says nothing about reliability.
entries.quote: Single runs do not estimate reliability.

entries.claim: No release has a measured speed or token saving; 2.3.0 states it explicitly.
entries.quote: No runtime benchmark was run for this release.
